statusText: Yellow / WATCH. Tail 24% sits at the top of the watch band and below the block threshold, while Stress 57% is elevated on a 2007-high Treasury selloff and crude above $100.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: WATCH. A narrow danger window is flagged across the 19:00-20:15 UTC power hour and cash close, where late-session continuation risk is highest. Outside that window the observed price path retains two-way character.
headline: Rate-driven Nasdaq-100 pullback stays orderly as the 10-year yield reaches its highest level since 2007
body: The Nasdaq-100 trades at 30,464.08, down 268.31 points (-0.87%) from a 30,732.40 previous close, within a 30,353.88-30,706.23 session range. The index has rebounded roughly 110 points off the session low rather than holding the extreme, and VIX at 15.04 (+5.85%) sits below its own 15.45 session high. The driver is the bond market: the 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.12-5.13%, its highest since 2007, with the 2-year at 4.91% and the 30-year near 5.37% in an approximately 16 basis point parallel selloff. September flash PMIs surprised strongly to the upside, with manufacturing at 57 against a 53.6 consensus and services at 58.7, and S&P Global reported input costs rising at the steepest rate in four years. Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr signalled that additional hikes are needed to address sticky inflation, lifting October hike pricing into a 60-75% range one week after the Fed raised its target range to 3.75-4.00%. Energy is the second channel: Brent moved above $100 and WTI above $92 after a cargo vessel was struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, while Iran separately floated conditions for reopening the waterway. Latest-session cross-asset context shows semiconductors uniformly negative with a -2.0% mean and six of eight megacaps lower, though software industries remained marginally positive and Meta and Microsoft held gains, so the decline is a rates-and-semis story rather than uniform liquidation. That dispersion, the observed rebound off the session low and a VIX of 15 are why elevated Stress is not accompanied by a blocking Tail score.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours began with a trend-up regime carrying Tail near 20% into the 22 September US close, then decayed steadily through the Asian and European sessions to a Tail low of 10-12% with a normal dominant mode. Conditions changed from roughly 12:00 UTC on 23 September as the Treasury selloff accelerated: Tail reached 25% and a trend-down mode at 14:00 UTC, the only blocking hour of the window, before easing to a 22-24% mixed regime as the index retraced off its lows while Stress stayed elevated in the low-to-mid 50s.
outlookSummary: The near-term path is dominated by the 19:00-20:15 UTC power hour and cash close, the one window projected above the block threshold, because the 10-year yield is sitting at its session high without retracement and a delayed second equity leg remains a credible unresolved mechanism. Beyond the close, conditional Tail decays through the Globex and Asian sessions into the mid-to-high teens, with two-sided Strait of Hormuz headline flow the main overnight gap channel. Risk rebuilds modestly into 24 September around Initial Jobless Claims at 12:30 UTC, the 13:30 UTC cash open and New Home Sales at 14:00 UTC, peaking near 23% without reaching the blocking band, since on the inherited calibration a scheduled release raises stress and forecast dispersion before it raises tail. The projection returns toward 19-20% by the end of the horizon on the base case that the hawkish repricing is absorbed in an orderly, two-way fashion.
